messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from this morning's RFC readthrough — proposing we split autoscaler responsibilities: central control-plane decides long-term capacity (+billing/cost signals) and per-pool sidecars handle short-term admission/backpressure and warmup. Thoughts?

ajay: Love the separation in theory. Main worry: split ownership adds two failure modes and more coordination. How do we keep global objectives (cost fairness, SLO weighting) from diverging across sidecars? :thinking:

maria: Good point. My sketch: control-plane publishes 'intent bundles' every 30s with target headroom and budget tokens; sidecars consume intent, enforce local admission, report back lease deficits. If mismatch crosses threshold, control-plane triggers corrective scaling.

kevin: Can you show a tiny config sketch? makes it concrete for operator impl.

maria: Sure — rough example:

```yaml
autoscaler: 
  mode: split
  intent_publish_interval: 30s
  budget_policy: cost-aware
  fallback: scale-up
sidecar: 
  admission_rate_limiter: token-bucket
  prewarm_policy: soft-lease
  telemetry_report_interval: 15s
```

jen: Two practical Qs: 1) telemetry volume — sidecars reporting every 15s from thousands of pools could be heavy. 2) What metrics do we use to decide corrective scaling vs local admission?

maria: For telemetry we only send compact aggregates: inflight_count, queue_depth, p95_startup, lease_deficit, recent_evicts. Expect ~6 values per sidecar. Use delta compression + periodic heartbeat.

ajay: For decision rules I'd prefer thresholds: if lease_deficit_rate > 5% over 2 mins AND p95_startup > target*1.5 => escalate scale-up. Otherwise sidecar shapes traffic with token-bucket. Avoid oscillation with a 3-min cool-down.

kevin: How does this interact with dedicated vs best-effort pools? We have tenants on dedicated committed capacity — they shouldn't be subject to same token draining.
maria: Intent bundles include a tenant_tier tag. Sidecars enforce tier-specific headroom. For dedicated pools intent will be 'reserve-x' and admission should be strict; best-effort gets cost-aware preemption hints.

jen: Rollout plan? We should be able to A/B on small set of pools and measure cost and latency impact. Also need a kill-switch.
maria: Proposed rollout steps:
- Canary 5 pools with low criticality and synthetic load tests
- Monitor: p50/p95 latency, cold-start rate, cost per token, failed admissions
- If regressions > 3% p95 or cold-starts increase by 10% => rollback

ajay: Ops questions: operator liveness and split-brain. If sidecar loses contact with control-plane, it must degrade safely — maybe go into local-pass-through admission conservative mode. Also add a lease TTL so stale intents don't allow unlimited admission.

maria: Agreed. Sidecar fallback semantics: conservative-mode = tighten token bucket to 30% of last intent headroom + disable prewarm. Also sidecars should emit an incident event to orch-bot.

orch-bot: Incident stub: sidecar lost control-plane connection (pool: pool-42). Autoalert created.

kevin: Testing: we need a harness to simulate mismatch scenarios (control-plane lag, burst loads, telemetry loss). Can we reuse the existing autoscale-sim harness?
maria: Yes, extend autoscale-sim to support split-mode and inject latency on bundle publish. We'll add evaluation scripts to compute cost-per-successful-request and fairness index (Jain's fairness over tenant latency).

jen: One last tradeoff note: split-mode gives lower tail latency during bursts (local decision + prewarm) but increases implementation surface and makes reasoning about global cost harder. We should ensure the control-plane has a conservative cost guardrail that can forcibly throttle sidecars if spend spikes.

maria: Exactly — plan: implement throttling API (control-plane -> sidecar) and a monitoring rule that triggers a global throttle if spend exceeds X% above forecast for 10m.

ajay: Sounds actionable. Can you open a follow-up RFC PR with the state machine diagram, minimal wire-format for intent bundles, and the test plan? I'll review and add operator concerns.

maria: Will do. PR will include: state transitions, minimal JSON intent schema, telemetry spec, and a rollout checklist. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

kevin: tagging for visibility — @jen (SRE) please add telemetry budget estimate to infra roadmap.

jen: On it. I'll post cost estimate by EOD tomorrow.
